speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are a 34-year-old male with a history of AIDS presenting with decreased vision and black spots in your right eye. To determine if this is related to your HIV status, have you noticed any floaters, flashes of light, or a shadow in your vision? Additionally, have you experienced any recent flu-like symptoms or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of AIDS, fungal esophagitis, and Kaposi's sarcoma, could you tell me if you have experienced any night sweats, weight loss, or fevers recently? I am also concerned about retinal pathology, so please wait while I order a retinal examination and an HIV viral load test. REQUEST TEST: HIV_Viral_Load, REQUEST TEST: CD4_Count, REQUEST IMAGES: Fundus_Photos_Right_Eye

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: HIV_Viral_Load: Not Detected; CD4_Count: 36/mm3; Fundus_Photos_Right_Eye: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages.

speaker: Doctor
text: With a CD4 count of 36/mm³ and fundus photos showing granular yellow-white opacities with hemorrhages, have you noticed any pain, photophobia, or floaters in the affected eye, and are you currently on any antiretroviral therapy?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fundus findings of granular yellow-white opacities ("cotton wool spots") combined with dot-blot hemorrhages in the setting of severe immunosuppression (CD4 < 50) are highly suggestive of Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis, though we must rule out other opportunistic infections. Have you had any recent history of fatigue, muscle aches, or a rash? REQUEST TEST: CMV_IgG, REQUEST TEST: Fungal_Cultures

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: CMV Retinitis. The combination of severe immunosuppression (CD4 count of 36/mm³), positive CMV IgG serology, and fundoscopic findings of granular yellow-white opacities with hemorrhages in an AIDS patient confirms this diagnosis. Given the negative fungal cultures and lack of pain, opportunistic fungal infections or uveitis are less likely.
